why: A register stating a number the gate measured differently is the failure this was ported for: strictNullChecks in src/ was reported as ZERO for seven consecutive rounds after it had gone back to seven. This break reproduces it.

A tautology is an absent assertion wearing a real one's clothes. The digest cannot see it -- equal(hp, maxHp) and equal(hp, hp) have the same argument shape -- so it needs its own rule.

why: ESLint prints NOTHING and exits 0 for a file no config block matches, so `npm run lint` can report success while whole directories are never linted. THE `creates` FIELD NAMED `.ts` WHILE THE BREAK WROTE `.jsx` UNTIL THIS WAS CAUGHT -- the restore removed a path that did not exist and left the real probe behind, where `check:coverage` found it on the next clean run. A restore is only as good as its list.
A renumbered row leaves a gap in a register whose whole value is that every known gap is enumerated. Demonstrated by the gate auditor: 'has no row 6', exit 1.

A ceiling that cannot refuse a rise is not a ceiling. Demonstrated by the gate auditor: eight `any`s took it to 135 against a ceiling of 131, exit 1.

why: I have not constructed a break for this one either. A test that reads the wall clock must be caught, and I have not watched that happen.

Deleting a test file must drop a floor. Demonstrated by the gate auditor, who probed ten candidate files and found every one dropped a floor -- so the net holds, but it holds because the floors are tight, not because the suite count is. **It DELETES a tracked file, so it declares it in `touches`** -- the surgical restore only puts back what an entry names, and the first version of this one left the test file deleted in the working tree.

A gate that REGENERATES the thing it checks can never fail. This one generates to a temp directory and diffs, so corrupting a committed generated value must be refused. It was not, before rule 13: the check rewrote the file and reported ok. **REQUIRES GODOT.** CI found this the first time the gate ran there: without Godot the gate NOTICEs and exits 0, so this break produced no failure and the self-test reported "the gate stayed GREEN" -- which reads as a gate defect and is a missing dependency.
